hints: Acceleration during the first 10 seconds is the gradient of the velocity-time graph from $t = 0$ to $t = 10\text{ s}$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the acceleration from the gradient of the graph during the first $10\text{ s}$:
$$a = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \frac{5 - 0}{10} = 0.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
On a velocity-time graph, uniform acceleration equals the gradient of the line:
$$a = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \frac{v_2 - v_1}{t_2 - t_1}$$

Substitute $v_1 = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at $t_1 = 0\text{ s}$, and $v_2 = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at $t_2 = 10\text{ s}$:
$$a = \frac{5 - 0}{10 - 0} = \frac{5}{10} = 0.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

hints: Calculate the area under each section of the velocity-time graph from $t = 0$ to $t = 90\text{ s}$.
Sum the five areas: triangle $\frac{1}{2}(10)(5)$, rectangle $20(5)$, trapezium $10\left(\frac{5+V}{2}\right)$, rectangle $30V$, and triangle $\frac{1}{2}(20)V$.
Simplify the sum to show that distance $= 150 + 45V$, then equate to $465\text{ m}$ to solve for $V$.
walkthrough:
Sum the areas under the velocity-time graph for all five sections:
$$\text{Distance} = \frac{1}{2}(10)(5) + (30-10)(5) + 10\left(\frac{5+V}{2}\right) + (70-40)V + \frac{1}{2}(90-70)V$$
$$\text{Distance} = 25 + 100 + 5(5+V) + 30V + 10V = 125 + 25 + 5V + 40V = 150 + 45V$$

Equate the total distance to $465\text{ m}$ and solve for $V$:
$$150 + 45V = 465 \implies 45V = 315 \implies V = \frac{315}{45} = 7\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough: The total distance travelled is found by calculating the area under each segment of the $v$-$t$ graph:

1. Segment 1 ($0 \le t \le 10$): Triangle of base $10$ and height $5$:
$$\text{Area}_1 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 5 = 25\text{ m}$$

2. Segment 2 ($10 \le t \le 30$): Rectangle of width $20$ and height $5$:
$$\text{Area}_2 = 20 \times 5 = 100\text{ m}$$

3. Segment 3 ($30 \le t \le 40$): Trapezium of parallel sides $5$ and $V$, and width $10$:
$$\text{Area}_3 = \frac{5 + V}{2} \times 10 = 5(5 + V) = 25 + 5V\text{ m}$$

4. Segment 4 ($40 \le t \le 70$): Rectangle of width $30$ and height $V$:
$$\text{Area}_4 = 30 \times V = 30V\text{ m}$$

5. Segment 5 ($70 \le t \le 90$): Triangle of base $20$ and height $V$:
$$\text{Area}_5 = \frac{1}{2} \times 20 \times V = 10V\text{ m}$$

Add all five areas together:
$$\text{Total distance} = 25 + 100 + 25 + 5V + 30V + 10V = 150 + 45V\text{ m}$$

We are given that the total distance is $465\text{ m}$. Set up the linear equation:
$$150 + 45V = 465$$
$$45V = 465 - 150 = 315$$
$$V = \frac{315}{45} = 7\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

hints: Calculate the gain in kinetic energy during the 10 seconds: $\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}m(V^2 - 5^2)$ with $m = 80\text{ kg}$ and $V = 7\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate the distance travelled in this stage using the average speed: $d = \left(\frac{5+7}{2}\right)(10) = 60\text{ m}$, then find work against resistance $W_{\text{res}} = 20 \times 60$.
Apply the work-energy balance for descending the slope: potential energy loss equals kinetic energy gain plus work against resistance, $mgh = \Delta E_k + W_{\text{res}}$, and solve for $h$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the gain in kinetic energy between $t = 30$ and $t = 40\text{ s}$:
$$\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}(80)(7^2) - \frac{1}{2}(80)(5^2) = 40(49 - 25) = 40(24) = 960\text{ J}$$

Calculate the distance travelled and the work done against resistance during this $10\text{ s}$ stage:
$$d = \left(\frac{5 + 7}{2}\right)(10) = 60\text{ m}, \quad W_{\text{res}} = 20 \times 60 = 1200\text{ J}$$

Apply the work-energy balance: loss in potential energy supplies the gain in kinetic energy and overcomes resistance:
$$mgh = \Delta E_k + W_{\text{res}} \implies 80(10)h = 960 + 1200 \implies 800h = 2160$$

Solve for the vertical height $h$:
$$h = \frac{2160}{800} = 2.7\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Between $t = 30\text{ s}$ and $t = 40\text{ s}$, the cyclist accelerates down the hill from speed $u = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $v = 7\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Calculate the increase in kinetic energy of the combined cyclist and bicycle ($m = 80\text{ kg}$):
$$\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}m(v^2 - u^2) = \frac{1}{2} \times 80 \times (7^2 - 5^2) = 40 \times (49 - 25) = 40 \times 24 = 960\text{ J}$$

Find the distance travelled down the incline during this $10\text{ s}$ interval:
$$d = \left(\frac{u + v}{2}\right) \times t = \left(\frac{5 + 7}{2}\right) \times 10 = 6 \times 10 = 60\text{ m}$$

Calculate the work done against the constant resistance force ($20\text{ N}$):
$$W_{\text{resistance}} = F_{\text{res}} \times d = 20 \times 60 = 1200\text{ J}$$

By the work-energy principle, the loss of gravitational potential energy equals the gain in kinetic energy plus the work done against resistance:
$$\text{PE loss} = \Delta E_k + W_{\text{resistance}}$$
$$mgh = 960 + 1200$$
$$80 \times 10 \times h = 2160$$
$$800h = 2160$$

Divide both sides by $800$ to find the vertical height $h$:
$$h = \frac{2160}{800} = \frac{27}{10} = 2.7\text{ m}$$
